questions.q: The expression $2^{4 n}-15 n-1$, where $n \in \mathbb{N}$ (the set of natural numbers) is divisible by
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  2^{4 n}-15 n-1=(1+15)^n-15 n-1=\left({ }^n C_0+{ }^n C_1 \cdot 15+{ }^n C_2 15^2+\ldots \ldots \ldots . .+{ }^n C_n \cdot 15^n\right)-15 n-1 \\ & =15^2\left({ }^n C_2+{ }^n C_3 \cdot 15 \ldots \ldots \ldots .+{ }^n C_n \cdot 15^{n-2}\right) \\ & =225 K, K \in \mathbb{N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ and $d$ be any four real numbers. Then. $a^{n}+b^{n}=c^{n}+d^{n}$ holds for any natural number $n$. if
questions.solution:
From option (d), we have
$\begin{aligned} \\ a-b &=c-d \\ \\ a^{2}-b^{2} &=c^{2}-d^{2} \\ \end{aligned}$
Consider, $a^{2}-b^{2}=c^{2}-d^{2}$
$\Rightarrow(a+b)(a-b)=(c-d)(c+d)$
$\Rightarrow \quad a+b=c+d$
On adding Eqs we get
$2 a=2 c \Rightarrow a=c$
$\Rightarrow \quad b=d$
Thus, $a^{n}+b^{n}=c^{n}+d^{n}$ for all $n \in N$

questions.q: The remainder obtained when $1 !+2 !+3 !+\ldots+11 !$ is divided by 12 is
questions.solution:
Let $S=1!+2 !+3 !+41+\ldots+11 !$
Here, we see that from $4 !$ to $111,$ we alwars get 12 factor, so it is always divisible by 12
Now. $1 !+2 !+3 !=1+2+6=9$
Hence, when $S$ is divided by $12,$ the remainder is 9.
